questions: Have you had this head tilt for as long as you can remember?
Is the double vision worse when you look down, such as when reading or going down stairs?
Have you had any recent head injury or trauma?
Do you have diabetes or high blood pressure?
Do you have any drooping of your eyelids?
Does the double vision worsen as the day goes on?
Do you see images tilted or rotated?
Do you have any pain with eye movement or around the eye?
Have you noticed any bulging of your eyes?

results: 1. Cover test to assess ocular deviation in primary and cardinal gazes
skew deviation / alternating cover test: skew deviation with LATERAL ALTERNATION - right eye hypotropic, left eye hypertropic
2. Three-step test (Parks-Bielschowsky) to identify the paretic extraocular muscle
ocular torsion and head tilt: RIGHT-sided head tilt; right eye excyclotorted and left eye incyclotorted - the complete ocular tilt reaction

MRI brain with gadolinium: left rostral pontine and caudal mesencephalic infarcts without enhancement
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Ocular tilt reaction due to left pontomesencephalic (lower brainstem) stroke - left-sided lesion involving the graviceptive pathways in the rostral pontine and caudal mesencephalic tegmentum, causing a right head tilt with right eye excyclotorsion and left eye incyclotorsion.
